question: Through the bridge, do two research flies living in separate worlds with different clocks perceive and respond to each other, and does a live (contingent) encounter differ from watching a recording of one?

hypotheses.E1: Subject A responds to B: the share of live A subjects that escape at least once exceeds the solitary D subjects'. Supported when the 95% Newcombe interval of live A − solitary D lies wholly above 0 and the other fly was seen in at least the criterion share of live sessions.
hypotheses.E2: The response runs both ways: the same for live B against solitary D.
hypotheses.E3: Contingency matters: live A differs from yoked C, who saw the same recorded motion without being able to change it. Supported when the interval of live A − yoked C excludes 0 (either sign).
